title: AutoGen .NET Multi-Agent Patterns
description: Use multi-agent conversation patterns with AutoGen-style collaboration, routing, and result aggregation in .NET.

blocks.text: Multi-agent systems assign different roles to different agents and let them collaborate through conversation. This is useful when a task has distinct phases: research, drafting, review, or validation.

blocks.title: Common roles
items: **Writer** — drafts answers or code from research.
**Router** — decides which agent should act next.
**User proxy** — represents human input or approval gates.

blocks.title: Keep agent responsibilities separate
blocks.text: Each agent should have a clear purpose, defined inputs, and expected outputs. Overlapping responsibilities create inconsistent behavior.

blocks.title: Design a Multi-Agent Workflow
blocks.description: Design a multi-agent system for a real backend task such as support triage or incident summarization.
steps: Define the end-to-end task and required outputs.
Define conversation flow or handoff rules.
Identify metrics for evaluating the multi-agent result.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should have a clear agent map, communication contract, and evaluation criteria.
